title: A Few GPUs, A Whole Lotta Scale: Faithful LLM Training Emulation with CrystalLLM
note: Preprint titled PrismLLM. Emulates thousand-GPU LLM training by running only selected ranks for real and replaying the rest as virtual participants - that hybrid emulation is exactly a single-GPU scale-down. Concern: fidelity claims are validated against real production clusters we cannot access and it builds on CRIU/cuda-checkpoint which may want privileges. No artifact link in the preprint.

title: FactorJoin: A New Cardinality Estimation Framework for Join Queries
note: Factor-graph cardinality estimator for joins - learned/statistical component inside the optimizer; runs on CPU with public benchmarks

title: Declarative Sub-Operators for Universal Data Processing
note: MLIR-based sub-operator IR and compiler in LingoDB; C++/LLVM builds in user space, CPU-only

title: Deterministic Client: Enforcing Determinism on Untrusted Machine Code
note: Pure user-space SFI-style verifier/rewriter and sandbox runtime for x86-64 machine code, evaluated with SPEC-style CPU benchmarks and a smart-contract engine; no kernel, no hypervisor, no counters needed. Concerns: builds on a patched LLVM (long user-space build); the Arm64 half cannot be evaluated on this x86 host; the paper did not participate in artifact evaluation, but the authors' repo is public and self-described as the research artifact.

title: Embracing Imbalance: Dynamic Load Shifting among Microservice Containers in Shared Clusters
note: Dynamic load shifting among microservice containers instead of load balancing - policy is trace/simulation friendly; concern: original evaluation is on a large shared cluster and no official repo was found

title: MaxK-GNN: Extremely Fast GPU Kernel Design for Accelerating Graph Neural Networks Training
note: Single-GPU SpGEMM/SSpMM kernels plus a nonlinearity for GNN training; Ampere-class GPU is the target. Fits the machine directly.

title: Bw-Graph: An Efficient Graph Storage System Harmonizing Topology-Aware Tree with Paged CSR
note: graph storage engine combining paged CSR with append-only delta pages and non-blocking structure modification - storage-engine design with an open artifact

title: ScaleOPT: A Scalable Optimal Page Replacement Policy Simulator
note: Parallel trace-driven simulator for Belady/OPT page replacement; plain C, CPU-only, compares directly against libCacheSim and webcachesim. Runs entirely in user space on cache traces. Concerns: evaluated on a 72-core machine, so our 16-core/32-thread CPU is a meaningful scale-down (speedup ceiling will be lower); repo has had no pushes since Oct 2024 and the ACM paper is closed-access so the trace list must be recovered from the repo.

title: LOOPRAG: Enhancing Loop Transformation Optimization with Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
note: Retrieval-augmented LLM loop transformation with compile-and-check validation; CPU-only pipeline

title: ByteCheckpoint: A Unified Checkpointing System for Large Foundation Model Development
note: Checkpoint save/load/resharding is fundamentally an I/O and serialization problem; the repo is a pip-installable PyTorch library with unit tests and demos. Ranks can be emulated with several processes over gloo/NCCL on one GPU or on CPU, and ~257 GB of NVMe is enough for sub-1B-parameter checkpoints. Concerns: the paper's headline numbers come from thousands of GPUs and remote object storage; single-node scale-down measures the resharding/serialization path only, not cluster-wide save throughput.

title: On Latency Predictors for Neural Architecture Search
note: Learned hardware-latency predictors (device representations, sample selection, operation encodings) trained on published latency datasets - an ML-for-systems artifact that fits one GPU comfortably. Concern - the URL printed in the paper (abdelfattah-lab/nasflat) 404s; the live lab repo nasflat_latency is the released code and should be confirmed at audit. The contribution is measured with prediction-accuracy metrics rather than system throughput.

title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
note: Chunked-prefill scheduling to trade throughput vs latency in LLM serving - pure user-space Python on top of vLLM. Paper used A100/A40 but a 7B model in FP16 fits the 24 GB A5000 so single-GPU scale-down is natural

title: SkyPIE: A Fast & Accurate Oracle for Object Placement
note: Precomputed placement-policy oracle evaluated on traces - policy/placement work that runs offline on one machine. Concern: the repo ships Docker instructions, so deps must be reproduced by hand with conda/cargo

title: Cardinality Estimation of LIKE Predicate Queries using Deep Learning
note: Learned cardinality estimator inside the query optimizer; CPU/GPU training fits one node

title: What Modern NVMe Storage Can Do, And How To Exploit It: High-Performance I/O for High-Performance Storage Engines
note: User-space high-IOPS NVMe I/O engine (io_uring, many threads) for storage engines; no root needed. Concern: paper uses 8 enterprise SSDs, we have 2 PM9A3 in software RAID so absolute IOPS will be lower. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/leanstore/leanstore/tree/io .

title: DumpKV: Learning based lifetime aware garbage collection for key value separation in LSM-tree
note: Learning-based lifetime-aware garbage collection for KV-separated LSM stores built on RocksDB; single node, disk-bound

title: Punica: Multi-Tenant LoRA Serving
note: Multi-tenant LoRA serving; the core artifact is the SGMV CUDA kernel plus a batching/scheduling layer, both of which work on one GPU. Concern - the paper's scheduler evaluation uses a small GPU cluster; on a single 24 GB A5000 the scale-down is a 7B base model with many adapters. Kernels are sm_80+ Ampere-friendly.

title: DarwinGame: Playing Tournaments for Tuning Applications in Noisy Cloud Environments
note: DarwinGame is a user-space performance tuner that runs tournaments between configurations under interference - interference can be emulated by co-located processes on one machine; Zenodo artifact released

title: SeLeP: Learning Based Semantic Prefetching for Exploratory Database Workloads
note: learned semantic prefetcher for exploratory database workloads

title: Kivi: Verification for Cluster Management
note: Model checker for Kubernetes controllers and configurations; the artifact is a user-space Python plus model-checking toolchain and the state-space reduction is a clean performance target. Concern: verification tooling rather than a classic OS topic, and the released artifact only earned the Available badge

title: Rubick: Exploiting Job Reconfigurability for Deep Learning Cluster Scheduling
note: DL cluster scheduler exploiting job reconfigurability - artifact ships a cluster simulator driven by pre-measured throughput tables so the scheduling policy can be studied without the 64-GPU cluster - concerns: repo is named Morphling, AE path assumes Docker but conda setup instructions are also provided

title: Efficiently Processing Joins and Grouped Aggregations on GPUs
note: GPU join and group-by operator optimizations; single GPU, fits a 24 GB A5000

title: Luci: Loader-based Dynamic Software Updates for Off-the-shelf Shared Objects
note: A drop-in user-space dynamic linker/loader that hot-patches unmodified Debian/Ubuntu shared objects - no kernel changes, no root, and the target distro family (Debian 12) matches the machine. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced, eval harness at https://github.com/luci-project/eval-atc23. Concerns: the AE workflow ships an Ubuntu VM image (ubuntu.ova) for convenience; without KVM that path is unusable, so Luci would have to be run natively on Debian 12 instead.

title: SymphonyQG: Towards Symphonious Integration of Quantization and Graph for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: SIMD-friendly integration of quantization and graph ANN index; CPU-only, cache/memory-access focused

title: Efficient GPU-Centric Evolving Graph Processing at Scale
note: Single-GPU out-of-core graph analytics; the artifact appendix says it was evaluated on an **NVIDIA RTX A4000**, i.e. a smaller Ampere card than ours. Concern: artifact asks for CUDA Toolkit >= 12.4 while the system nvcc is 11.8 and the driver is 535 - a per-user conda CUDA 12.4 toolkit is needed and minor-version compatibility must hold

title: Sample-Efficient Cardinality Estimation Using Geometric Deep Learning
note: geometric deep learning cardinality estimator with an end-to-end PostgreSQL benchmark

title: TiDedup: A New Distributed Deduplication Architecture for Ceph
note: Deduplication (selective crawling, content-defined chunking, shared reference back pointers) is squarely in the storage topic, and Ceph OSDs are user-space daemons that vstart.sh can run as a single-node cluster without root. Merged into the Ceph mainline, so the code is unambiguously released. Concerns: building Ceph is a heavy source build whose install-deps.sh normally wants apt/root - every dependency would have to be satisfied via conda or vendored submodules; this is the main feasibility risk. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/ssdohammer-sl/ceph/tree/tidedup .

title: PointShuffler: Accelerating Point Cloud Neural Networks on General-Purpose GPUs
note: GPU-friendly point cloud network inference - README confirms CUDA 11.8, PyTorch 2.1 and PyTorch CUDA extensions on a single GPU, pre-trained weights included. Strong fit

title: Adaptive Online Cache Capacity Optimization via Lightweight Working Set Size Estimation at Scale (Cuki)
note: Core artifact is a sketch-like data structure for online working-set-size / item-repetition-ratio / miss-ratio-curve estimation, plus an adaptive cache-capacity tuner - trace-driven cache work, exactly the caching topic, and AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the end-to-end numbers use Alluxio plus Presto (extra repos Cuki-Artifact-Alluxio, Cuki-Artifact-Presto) which are JVM-heavy and normally multi-node; the standalone estimator is trivially runnable on traces, which is the realistic project scope.

title: Sphinx: A Succinct Perfect Hash Index for x86
note: Succinct perfect-hash in-memory index for key-value stores tuned for commodity x86; user-space, memory-footprint driven

title: Cookie Monster: Efficient On-Device Budgeting for Differentially-Private Ad-Measurement Systems
note: Core artifact is a user-space on-device budget manager plus a Python/Rust trace-driven simulator over Criteo and microbenchmark datasets; runs CPU-only, no root. Clear quantitative objective (queries answerable per privacy budget) that an improvement hypothesis can target. Concern: privacy/utility rather than classic OS resource management - topic fit rests on the other-userspace catch-all.

title: LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention
note: Unified static plus dynamic sparse attention for long-context serving - Llama-3-8B fits 24 GB and the kernels are Ampere-compatible INT/FP16 - concern: shared OmniServe repo with QServe, and the longest-context configs assume 40-80 GB GPUs

title: Federated Fine-Tuning of Sparsely-Activated Large Language Models on Resource-Constrained Devices
note: Federated fine-tuning of MoE LLMs on consumer-grade GPUs. Concern: multiple participants would have to be simulated sequentially on the one A5000 and no code release was found

title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About Storage Compressibility of Pre-Trained ML Models but Were Afraid to Ask
note: deduplication and compression study of pre-trained model files; needs tens of GB of downloads but 257 GB free is enough

title: gSampler - General and Efficient GPU-based Graph Sampling for Graph Learning
note: Single-GPU matrix-centric graph sampler with a data-flow-graph optimizer; AE reference hardware is a single V100 so a 24 GB A5000 is comfortable, and everything is user-space PyTorch/DGL/CUDA. Concerns - the AE instructions ask for 256 GB RAM to preprocess ogbn-papers100M and Friendster in CSC format and we only have ~111 GB available, so the study must stay on ogbn-products and LiveJournal or use out-of-core preprocessing

title: ALECE: An Attention-based Learned Cardinality Estimator for SPJ Queries on Dynamic Workloads
note: learned cardinality estimator wired into PostgreSQL; single node, fits 24 GB GPU

title: Characterization and Reclamation of Frozen Garbage in Managed FaaS Workloads
note: Desiccant is a freeze-aware memory manager inside managed runtimes (JVM / Node.js) - user-space GC and heap work, buildable from source in $HOME. Concern - the FaaS harness around it likely assumes a container-based platform; the runtime changes themselves can be exercised with plain processes plus cgroup v2 memory limits

title: The FastLanes File Format
note: Open-source columnar file format with cascading lightweight data-parallel encodings; portable auto-vectorizing C++, single node

title: Predictive Translation: High-Performance Buffer Management Without the Trade-Offs
note: buffer manager that replaces pointer chasing with deterministic page placement, explicitly avoiding kernel modules - user-space memory management for larger-than-memory data - concern: no repo located

title: FlowLog: Efficient and Extensible Datalog via Incrementality
note: Datalog engine with a per-rule relational IR that separates recursion from logical planning; user-space Rust runtime and compiler work

title: PAT: Accelerating LLM Decoding via Prefix-Aware Attention with Resource Efficient Multi-Tile Kernel
note: Prefix-aware attention decode kernel; pure CUDA/Triton kernel work that runs on one Ampere GPU. Zenodo AE artifact 10.5281/zenodo.18217189

title: PATHFINDER: Practical Real-Time Learning for Data Prefetching
note: Spiking-neural-network data prefetcher evaluated in ChampSim, which is a CPU-only trace-driven simulator that runs fine here. Concern - the paper also has an RTL/hardware cost analysis that cannot be reproduced.

title: SeRF: Segment Graph for Range-Filtering Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Range-filtering ANN search index; CPU only, single node, modest memory

title: Two Birds With One Stone: Designing a Hybrid Cloud Storage Engine for HTAP
note: hybrid column-row cloud storage engine for HTAP. Concern: object-store experiments need a user-space substitute such as MinIO

title: On Reducing Space Amplification with Multi-Column Compaction in Apache IoTDB
note: multi-column LSM-tree compaction policy in Apache IoTDB; JVM, single node, classic storage project

title: Empower Vision Applications with LoRA LMM
note: Heterogeneous LoRA adapter batching operator and adapter orchestration for multimodal serving, built on LightLLM; LLaVA-7B class models fit in 24 GB. Concern - evaluated on A100s, so the adaptive-tiling kernel may need retuning for Ampere SM86, and adapter generation needs a fine-tuning step

title: Grafite: Taming Adversarial Queries with Optimal Range Filters
note: Range filter with worst-case guarantees, evaluated inside key-value workloads; CPU only

title: When Amnesia Strikes: Understanding and Reproducing Data Loss Bugs with Fault Injection
note: FUSE-based fault-injection file system; /dev/fuse is world-writable and fusermount3 is setuid so it runs unprivileged

title: Efficient Reproduction of Fault-Induced Failures in Distributed Systems with Feedback-Driven Fault Injection
note: Anduril is a user-space JVM-level fault-injection and search tool; targets (ZooKeeper, HDFS, Cassandra, Kafka) are normally run as several JVMs on a single host, which env.md explicitly allows. Efficiency metric (injections/time to reproduce a failure) is directly measurable. Concern: testing/debugging tooling, not resource management; 125 GiB RAM should hold the multi-JVM setups but runs are long.

title: OHMiner: An Overlap-centric System for Efficient Hypergraph Pattern Mining
note: CPU-only hypergraph pattern mining engine with a redundancy-free compiler; multi-core user space and fits comfortably in 125 GiB. Concern - some hypergraph datasets are large so memory footprint and download size should be checked before committing

title: In-Production Characterization of an Open Source Serverless Platform and New Scaling Strategies
note: Serverless scaling strategies evaluated against released production traces - trace-driven policy work explicitly in scope, artifact and traces are public

title: Bridging the GPU Utilization Gap: Predictive Multi-Dimensional Resource Scheduling for AI Workloads
note: Predictive multi-dimensional GPU resource scheduler - schedulers of this kind are normally evaluated with cluster traces and a simulator which fits here. Concerns: multi-tenant cluster target and no code found

title: Rethinking The Compaction Policies in LSM-trees
note: Compaction policy design in LSM-trees treating compaction as a resource investment; classic single-machine storage work

title: Are Joins over LSM-trees Ready: Take RocksDB as an Example
note: Systematic benchmark of join algorithms and secondary indexes over RocksDB; single-node disk-based LSM work with full code

title: Inductive Invariants That Spark Joy: Using Invariant Taxonomies to Streamline Distributed Protocol Proofs
note: Invariant taxonomy tool that streamlines distributed protocol proofs - Dafny toolchain runs entirely in user space on CPU. Concern - an improvement project here is proof automation rather than systems performance

title: Automated Tensor-Relational Decomposition for Large-Scale Sparse Tensor Computation
note: Automatic rewriting of Einstein-notation tensor computations into a tensor-relational form so sparsity is handled relationally and dense kernels do the math. Concern: the reference system targets large-scale sparse tensors so inputs must be scaled down

title: Reducing Energy Bloat in Large Model Training
note: Perseus's core is an offline time-energy Pareto planner over pipeline-stage frequency assignments - a graph algorithm that runs on profiles, so it can be studied and improved without the training cluster. Energy/power readings come from NVML via nvidia-smi, which needs no root and no perf counters. Concern: end-to-end validation in the paper uses multi-GPU pipeline-parallel training; on one A5000 only the planner plus single-GPU DVFS profiling is reproducible, and GPU frequency locking may require privileges. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/ml-energy/zeus/tree/kronos .

title: NeuroSketch: Fast and Approximate Evaluation of Range Aggregate Queries with Neural Networks
note: Neural network replacing range-aggregate query evaluation, with theory on when it works - a learned system component; small models fit the A5000 easily

title: DARQ Matter Binds Everything: Performant and Composable Cloud Programming via Resilient Steps
note: Resilient-step abstraction and speculative durability for composable cloud programs - a user-space runtime idea. Concern: evaluated as a distributed cloud service, so a single-host multi-process scale-down is needed; no artifact confirmed (possibly inside microsoft/FASTER)

title: F3: The Open-Source Data File Format for the Future
note: next-generation columnar file format with WebAssembly-embedded decoders - pure user-space storage/compression artifact that builds and runs on one node

title: NeurStore: Efficient In-database Deep Learning Model Management System
note: tensor-level deduplication plus delta quantization for storing DL models in a database - compression/dedup storage engine work

title: Cilantro: Performance-Aware Resource Allocation for General Objectives via Online Feedback
note: The contribution is an online-learning resource-allocation policy with confidence bounds - pure Python, simulatable from traces. Concern: every released experiment targets a Kubernetes/EKS cluster and ships a Dockerfile, and this machine has no root and no Docker, so the policies would have to be driven by a locally written trace-driven simulator or by cgroup-v2-limited processes.

title: FastServe: Iteration-Level Preemptive Scheduling for Large Language Model Inference
note: Iteration-level preemptive MLFQ scheduling for LLM serving plus GPU/host KV-cache swapping - the scheduler is the contribution and reproduces on one 24 GB GPU with a 7-8B model. Concern - paper is evaluated on a multi-GPU distributed deployment and the engine is a custom C++ stack rather than vLLM.

title: Apt-Serve: Adaptive Request Scheduling on Hybrid Cache for Scalable LLM Inference Serving
note: Request scheduling plus hybrid KV/hidden cache for LLM serving; directly on-topic and single-GPU friendly

title: Einsum Trees: An Abstraction for Optimizing the Execution of Tensor Expressions
note: Einsum Tree IR that globally optimizes data layout for tensor-contraction paths - CPU-only user-space compiler, evaluated on x86 desktop-class machines

title: ConfD: Analyzing Configuration Dependencies of File Systems for Fun and Profit
note: ConfD's core (taint analyzer, dependency analyzer, state generator) is LLVM-based static analysis of file-system source code - it runs entirely in user space with no root and no mounted file systems, and LLVM/clang is installable via conda. Concern: several of the six plugins validate findings by running xfstests and e2fsprogs against mounted ext4/XFS instances, which needs root; those plugins could not be reproduced, so a project here would have to target the static-analysis side (e.g. extending to more file systems, improving false-positive rate) rather than the mount-based validation.

title: Debunking the Myth of Join Ordering: Toward Robust SQL Analytics
note: Predicate transfer integrated into DuckDB for join-order robustness; single node, user space

title: FusionFlow: Accelerating Data Preprocessing for Machine Learning with CPU-GPU Cooperation
note: CPU-GPU cooperative data-preprocessing scheduler for DL training. Concern: multi-GPU results are not reproducible, single-GPU path is

title: CacheSlide: Unlocking Cross Position-Aware KV Cache Reuse for Accelerating LLM Serving
note: KV-cache reuse policy implemented as a vLLM 0.8.5 extension - pure user space + single GPU. Concern: paper uses A100 80 GB (70B model on 2 A100s); on a 24 GB A5000 only the 7-8B configs fit, so 70B results cannot be reproduced. FlashAttention-2 works on Ampere so the attention path is fine.

title: FairyWREN: A Sustainable Cache for Emerging Write-Read-Erase Flash Interfaces
note: Flash cache that co-designs admission/eviction with garbage collection - a CacheLib fork by the first author is public although the paper itself gives no code link. Concern - the WREN/FDP interface needs a capable SSD and the machine has no root for device configuration so the study would have to be simulation or emulation based on the released carbon and write-amplification models

title: GastCoCo: Graph Storage and Coroutine-Based Prefetch Co-Design for Dynamic Graph Processing
note: coroutine-based prefetching and graph storage co-design that targets cache misses; CPU only

title: Cache-Craft: Managing Chunk-Caches for Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation
note: KV-cache reuse for RAG chunks; core KV-cache management topic, single-GPU 7B-class models feasible

title: KPerfIR: Towards a Open and Compiler-centric Ecosystem for GPU Kernel Performance Tooling on Modern AI Workloads
note: Profiling implemented as Triton compiler passes (upstreamed into triton-lang/triton third_party/proton/dialect); instrumentation is intra-kernel clock-based, so it does not need perf or root. Concern: the motivating use case is warp-specialized overlap on Hopper; on an Ampere A5000 some passes may be inapplicable, and Triton builds usually want CUDA 12.x installed via conda rather than the system 11.8.

title: Aegaeon: Effective GPU Pooling for Concurrent LLM Serving on the Market
note: The core mechanism - token-granularity auto-scaling that multiplexes many models onto *one* GPU with fast weight swapping - is inherently a single-GPU idea and the paper itself includes a single-A10 experiment. Official artifact (first author Y. Xiang; also Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16673199). Concerns - the AE README asks for 2x8 H100 nodes, an A100-80GB node, ~512 GB CPU RAM and ~256 GB of model weights; a serious scale-down to a pool of small models on 24 GB is mandatory and the multi-node baselines cannot be reproduced.

title: Neutrino: Fine-grained GPU Kernel Profiling via Programmable Probing
note: Deliberately hardware-counter-free GPU profiler (assembly-layer probes, user-space driver interception), so perf_event_paranoid=3 and the lack of root are not blockers. Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concern: SASS probing is tied to specific driver/CUDA versions - needs checking against driver 535.216.01 and sm_86.

title: VClinic: A Portable and Efficient Framework for Fine-Grained Value Profilers
note: Dynamic-binary-instrumentation value profiler - user space no root or perf counters required  GitHub + Zenodo artifact

title: FlowWalker: A Memory-efficient and High-performance GPU-based Dynamic Graph Random Walk Framework
note: GPU dynamic-graph random-walk engine with sampler-centric scheduling; one GPU

title: Skyler: Static Analysis for Predicting API-Driven Costs in Serverless Applications
note: Static cost analysis tool for serverless applications; user-space Java/Python tooling. Concern: it is a static analyzer rather than a runtime system so the improvement axis is analysis precision

title: MAST: Towards Efficient Analytical Query Processing on Point Cloud Data
note: Approximate invocation of deep models for point-cloud analytical queries; single-GPU inference

title: TeraHeap: Reducing Memory Pressure in Managed Big Data Frameworks
note: Adds an NVMe-backed second heap to the JVM to cut GC pressure for Spark/Giraph - user-space OpenJDK build on one node  GitHub + Zenodo artifact
